auditor_notes: The Wikipedia 2000 PC candidate list entry for Ellery Hollingsworth in Scarborough Southwest (record B) says he served as a Scarborough Board of Education trustee from 1994 to 1997, which is the office won in record A's 1994 run.
second_check_notes: WebFetch of the Wikipedia list was refused (outside the fetch tool's allowed set), and a redirect to it found by one search was also blocked. The quotes were checked on the auditor's saved copy (canonical en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Progressive_Conservative_Party_of_Canada_candidates_in_the_2000_Canadian_federal_election, revision 1374003189, last edited 9 September 2026). The Scarborough Southwest entry reads 'Hollingsworth was 59 years old at the time of the election, and was a retired manager for the Canadian Broadcasting Corporation. He had also served as a school trustee on the Scarborough Board of Education from 1994 to 1997, following unsuccessful campaigns in 1988 and 1991.' and 'He received 5,251 votes (14.68%), finishing second against Liberal incumbent Tom Wappel.' The 5,251 votes match record B, and the trustee service from 1994 matches record A's 1994 Ward 7 win, the only Hollingsworth elected to that board in 1994. Office held is a distinctive fact, so the standard is met. Elections Canada's 2000 table gives P.C., Retired, which fits. The trustee and provincial splits review (trustee-provincial-splits-2026-10-29.md) compared only the 2006 Ward 18 record with the 2000 record and found no source. It did not consider the 1994 record, so its finding does not stand against this join. A caution for the other records: a Jeremy Hollingsworth and an Ellery Hollingsworth both ran for the TDSB in 2006, so they are two people, and the 1997 Jeremy Ellery Hollingsworth cannot be placed on name alone.
